registration.text:
Preregistration — Time pressure and moral judgment

Sample size. We will recruit 200 participants from Prolific, and data collection will stop once 200 complete responses are obtained.

Hypotheses. We predict that participants under time pressure will make more deontological judgments than participants in the control condition.

Manipulated variables. Time pressure will be manipulated between subjects: participants in the experimental condition will have 8 seconds to respond to each dilemma, while control participants will have unlimited time.

Exclusion criteria. We will exclude participants who fail more than one of three attention checks.

Statistical models. We will analyse the data using a 2 (time pressure: yes vs. no) x 2 (dilemma type) mixed ANOVA, with an alpha of .05.

paper.text:
Method

Participants. A total of 243 participants were recruited via Prolific. After exclusions, 218 participants remained in the final sample.

Hypotheses. We hypothesised that time pressure would increase deontological responding relative to the control condition.

Design and manipulation. Time pressure was manipulated between participants; those in the time-pressure condition were given 8 seconds per dilemma, whereas control participants responded at their own pace.

Exclusions. Participants who failed two or more of the three attention checks were excluded from analyses. We additionally excluded 7 participants for completing the study in under two minutes, a criterion that was not specified in our preregistration.

Analysis. Responses were analysed with a 2 (time pressure) x 2 (dilemma type) mixed ANOVA (alpha = .05). We also report an exploratory mediation analysis.
